kind: AI integration and programmable ReAct runtime

runtime.execution: Task-coordinated ReAct runner or Jido actor strategy; ReqLLM provider dependency, typed action modules, configurable concurrent tools.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns request/reasoning state and local retrieval memory, consumes provider/action/service dependencies; independent external kernel/DB lifecycle remains outside.

summary: Composable model request transforms, tool interceptors, steering and signed caller-owned continuation tokens; logical restore explicitly loses active process handles.

inspection.scope: request/stream loop, turn execution/tool batches, checkpoints/tokens, request transform/hooks, steering, retrieval and observable-event sanitization, direct test oracles
inspection.limits: ReqLLM/Jido.Action dependencies not populated here; no live model calls; no general automatic compaction/rebuild protocol established.

actions.name: Agent.ask / ask_stream / ask_sync / await
actions.output: request ID/handle, event stream or final result/error
actions.lifecycle: task/actor-backed model-tool loop; asynchronous handle tracked to terminal
actions.authority: application owns provider credentials and exposed action roster

actions.name: Turn.execute / execute_module
actions.input: tool name/module, params, context, timeout and action map
actions.lifecycle: await action; agent callbacks apply only in managed runtime, standalone bypass explicit
actions.authority: advertised typed action module and application context

actions.name: request_transformer.transform_request
actions.lifecycle: each model step; transformer participates in token fingerprint
actions.authority: authored module can redefine request; no implicit model permission needed

actions.name: before_tool_call / after_tool_call
actions.input: resolved tool identity+arguments/context or final retried result
actions.lifecycle: before validation/retries; after once final result; standalone bypasses callbacks
actions.authority: application agent module/effect policy; identity immutable

actions.name: steer / inject / cancel
actions.input: active actor/request ID, content/source/refs or reason
actions.lifecycle: steering drained at boundary; undrained best-effort input may drop; cancellation cooperative
actions.authority: expected request ID/source and application actor access

actions.name: ReAct.stream_from_state / rt2 Token.issue/decode_state
actions.lifecycle: after model/tools/terminal checkpoints; does not migrate active tasks
actions.authority: token secret and matching config fingerprint

actions.name: Retrieval.Store.upsert / recall / clear
actions.output: stored memory or token-overlap-ranked results/deletion count
actions.lifecycle: in-process ETS lifetime; no external DB lease implied

actions.name: AI agent checkpoint/restore sanitizer
actions.output: serializable state with interrupted stream error and idle strategy
actions.lifecycle: drops live handles; new runtime after restore

actions.name: Test.expect_react script
actions.input: user prompt, named tool calls and scripted answers
actions.output: deterministic provider boundary consumed by real runtime
actions.lifecycle: per test process tree or explicit script; no live provider
actions.authority: test author chooses expected sequence and must assert real output

filesystem.detail: Authored typed action modules can perform arbitrary application I/O/programs; no built-in unrestricted shell/kernel implied by tool execution.

processes.detail: Authored typed action modules can perform arbitrary application I/O/programs; no built-in unrestricted shell/kernel implied by tool execution.

code_actions.detail: Authored typed action modules can perform arbitrary application I/O/programs; no built-in unrestricted shell/kernel implied by tool execution.

persistent_kernel.detail: Long-lived actors and checkpoint state are logical state; active worker/process handles reset explicitly, not retained interpreter heap.

standing_database.detail: Retrieval memory is namespace ETS with token-overlap recall; no shared durable service standing DB contract from this store.

workflow_programming.detail: Reasoning strategies, per-turn request transforms and bounded concurrent action execution/interceptors are actual programmable orchestration.

multi_model.detail: Effective model can change in per-turn transformer; separate actor configurations/strategies can compose models through Jido runtime.

live_collaboration.detail: Inter-agent inject is a wired same-run input primitive; Jido actor messaging supplies peers, but a full live multi-model room/roster is application composition.

concurrent_work.detail: Monitored runner tasks and bounded concurrent tools with original order results; timeouts/retries bound rounds, not remote transaction settlement.

steering_interrupt.detail: Request-scoped cancel and steer/inject are real; steering can be dropped before drain and cancellation checks do not undo or universally stop external action effects.

turn_redefinition.detail: Request transforms control model/messages/tools/options; agent before/after tool callbacks control arguments/results/effects. Identity restrictions and standalone bypass are explicit.

compaction.detail: Transformer can replace model messages; inspected core does not supply managed summarization with original archive/semantic fidelity oracle.

context_repair.detail: Caller-owned continuation state and request message transform can rebuild context; redacted/truncated telemetry alone cannot restore lost originals.

original_audit.detail: Identified sequence events/checkpoints and context capture are useful, but sanitization/redaction/truncation and configured delta capture prevent all-byte audit claim.

audit_query.detail: Consumer receives identified events/checkpoint tokens; telemetry/result inspection external composition, not queryable all-original core DB.

hot_change.detail: Per-turn transformer redefines effective request; checkpoint token fingerprint rejects changed model/transformer config rather than silently accepting arbitrary hot program replacement.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Signed tokens support caller-owned completed-boundary continuation; logical actor checkpoint removes live worker/stream handles and interrupted requests fail. No effect-settled refit/outpost.

remote_services.detail: ReqLLM provider stream/generate integration and authored action service calls; ownership stays with independently configured service.

self_improvement.detail: Transformers/actions/test scripts can support controlled experiments; no model-governed hypothesis/promotion loop in inspected runtime.

complaints.detail: Structured interceptor/provider/runtime errors and attributed events useful for complaints, but no full-state externally tracked bead action traced.

authority.detail: Named action roster, preflight, effect/interceptor policies and signed/fingerprinted continuation token; not mandatory per-command operator approval.

evaluation.detail: Scripted provider and direct checkpoint/signature/steering assertions test actual state transitions with mocked model boundary; not semantic model or external side-effect oracle.

time_order.detail: Event IDs/monotonic seq; ordered concurrent tool output and heartbeat sequence adoption; checkpoint emitted before terminal to avoid lost final state.

evidence.claim: Runner starts monitored task and streamed events; stream_from_state appends new input to checkpoint state.
Stream/generate provider dispatch via ReqLLM; scripted testing boundary uses same consumption path.
Tool name map resolves authored action module, timeout/context/options passed to execution; missing tool produces structured error.
Tool preflight, active tool map, ordered bounded concurrent Task.async_stream with retries; heartbeat sequence range adopted before completion events.
Before interceptor can change arguments or interrupt, not action identity; after interceptor changes result/effects once after retries; standalone Turn execution does not use agent callbacks.
Per-turn request transformer overrides messages/tools/model/options and validates effective request; errors/exceptions structured.
Public cancel emits request-scoped signal; steer/inject target active run with best-effort queue and explicitly drop if never drained before termination.
Drain injects attributed input into same state/context and emits input_injected; incomplete blank terminal responses rejected.
Signed rt2 token includes run/request IDs, minimal state, config fingerprint, issuance/expiration; validates before continuation and can mark checkpoint canceled.
Checkpoint issued after model/tools/terminal; terminal token emitted before terminal event and sink closure. Events monotonic seq/run/request/iteration identities.
Logical agent checkpoints remove request stream sinks/worker processes and reset interrupted runs to idle; interrupted streamed request recorded failed.
Local namespace ETS memory upsert/recall/clear; retrieval is token-overlap ranking, not external durable vector/SQL service.
Observation applies sensitive redaction, payload summaries and truncation markers; telemetry projection is not a complete original archive.
Tool args can be redacted and cancel is cooperative check of request ref; stopping underlying external action effect requires its implementation.
Direct oracle asserts failed interrupted stream, no process-local handles, term serialization and restored idle state with new task supervisor.
Token tampering/model/request-transformer mismatch rejected; config fingerprint deliberately constrains reuse under changed program.
Mock provider observes next request containing Q1/Q2 and prior A1; original request yields A2, idle inject rejected.
Public deterministic model scripts exercise actual ReAct/tools/event projection without claiming live model correctness.

tests.oracle: Exact stream_interrupted/failed/idle states, no runtime handles and roundtrip serializable payload; old active request does not magically resume.
Tampered signature and changed model/transformer produce exact errors; no proof of physical external task settlement.
Stubbed provider captures exact user/assistant messages on second call; original handle resolves A2 and idle inject rejects.

strengths: Request/response/tool transform program hooks are substantial agency surfaces.
Explicitly sanitizes dead process handles instead of fabricating active continuation.
Signed caller-owned tokens and monotonic boundary events make continuity contract testable.
limits: Local ETS retrieval is not shared durable computation.
Redacted bounded telemetry cannot serve complete original audit.
Config mismatch limits token reuse across program refit; cooperative cancellation and retries do not settle external effects.
arconaut_questions: How can a refit deliberately migrate/fingerprint logical state rather than merely reject changed config?
How should model-program hooks be authored/reloaded while retaining original inputs/results?
Should accepted steering return a durable delivery handle to avoid undrained input loss?
